pr.title: feat(rte): llm_runtime meta exposure + cell alias resolution (E4 finish)
pr.body:
## Summary
- Resolves `${ALIAS_NAME}` placeholders in `call_llm(model_id=...)` at the entry point via `run_extraction_v5.resolve_cell_alias()` so cells in model_map.yaml v3 can use aliases without leaking to the wire request.
- Surfaces `service_tier_requested` / `service_tier_observed` (from response usage), `cached_tokens` / `cache_write_tokens` (already captured in `_response_summary_metadata`), and `cache_strategy_applied` in the call_llm result meta dict so the orchestrator can pass them to spend_ledger.accumulate().
- Adds tests covering passthrough, override precedence (CLI > env > profile default), and meta exposure across OpenAI / OpenRouter / Anthropic-via-OR / Gemini / xAI response shapes.

## Scope
Limited to llm_runtime.py and three new test files. No changes to pricing.yaml, spend_ledger, batch_clients, structured_output_contracts, run_extraction_v5 cfg construction.

## Validation
New tests verify alias resolution and meta exposure. Existing cost cap + sidefill + repair counter tests remain green. RTE_DISABLE_LIVE_LLM_IN_TESTS=1 enforced.

## NOT_RUN
- Real provider calls.
- End-to-end orchestrator integration (covered by E7 packet).

## Residual Risks / UNKNOWNs
- service_tier_observed depends on providers honestly echoing the tier in response usage; OpenAI does, but OpenRouter passthrough behavior for tier echoes is unverified.
- Cell alias resolution happens at every call_llm entry, so each alias lookup costs one dict access per call (negligible).

@codex review

steps.task: Preflight: verify worktree, branch, clean state, and that TP-RTE-COSTPROFILE-E3-CONTRACTS-001 has merged (its changes are needed for cache_directives plumb-through).
validation: E3 packet commits visible in ancestry; otherwise STOP and rebase onto E3 merge.

steps.task: Locate alias-resolution insertion point in `call_llm()`. Verify the early-exit code path (live-LLM blocked, disabled_providers check) executes BEFORE alias resolution so blocked routes don't trigger alias lookups.
validation: Insertion point identified by line number.
Order is: live-LLM block → disabled_providers check → alias resolution → payload construction.

steps.task: Insert alias resolution at the top of call_llm() after the disabled_providers gate: `if model_id.startswith('${') and model_id.endswith('}'): from run_extraction_v5 import resolve_cell_alias; model_id = resolve_cell_alias(model_id, cost_profile=getattr(cfg, 'cost_profile', 'value-default'), cli_overrides=dict(getattr(cfg, 'model_alias_overrides', ())), env=os.environ)`. Add `_resolved_from_alias: bool` field to meta to surface that resolution happened.
validation: Resolution is lazy (only triggered when placeholder is detected).
Original model_id is preserved in meta as `model_id_requested` for debugging.
Cycle protection: if resolve_cell_alias returns another `${...}` placeholder, raise ValueError rather than recurse.

steps.task: Add the new meta fields. In the result-construction site at end of call_llm, ensure meta includes: `service_tier_requested` (from kwarg), `service_tier_observed` (from response_summary.usage.service_tier when present, else None), `cached_tokens` (already captured by _response_summary_metadata), `cache_write_tokens` (already captured), `cache_strategy_applied` (from prompt_cache_directives['strategy'] if applied else 'none'), `model_id_requested`, `_resolved_from_alias`.
validation: Meta dict has the 7 new fields after a successful call.
Existing meta fields are untouched (no rename, no type change).

steps.task: Plumb cached_tokens / cache_write_tokens / service_tier_requested through to the lifecycle_callback emissions so per-attempt telemetry includes them.
validation: Lifecycle callback receives `cached_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `service_tier_requested` keys when present.
Existing lifecycle consumers don't break when these keys are absent (e.g., during legacy provider calls).

steps.task: Write test_llm_runtime_service_tier_passthrough.py: mock OpenAI client; verify chat_kwargs receives service_tier when set; verify it's omitted for xAI provider even if set; verify meta['service_tier_requested'] = what caller passed; verify meta['service_tier_observed'] surfaces from mocked response.

Write test_llm_runtime_cell_alias_resolution.py: pass `model_id='${QUALITY_SYNTH_CRITICAL_MODEL}'`, mock cfg.cost_profile='quality'; verify resolved model_id passed to provider client; verify meta['_resolved_from_alias']=True and meta['model_id_requested']='${QUALITY_SYNTH_CRITICAL_MODEL}'; verify CLI override precedence; verify cycle detection raises.

Write test_llm_runtime_cached_tokens_meta.py: feed simulated OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini response usage shapes through `_response_summary_metadata`; assert cached_tokens is normalized correctly from each provider's native field name (OpenAI prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens, Anthropic cache_read_input_tokens, Gemini cached_content_token_count); assert cache_write_tokens captured from Anthropic only.
validation: 6+ tests pass; provider-specific edge cases (missing usage block, partial fields) covered.
